items.title: THREAD: Why every new NBA contract seems like an overpay.
items.body_excerpt:
THREAD: Why every new NBA contract seems like an overpay. 

First, it is hard to have a proper frame of reference when looking at the dollars. The cap keeps rising. 

This shows what a 30% max player would be in each season. A $32M a year player eight years ago is equivalent to $50m now.

images.alt:
Bar chart titled "What a 30% Max Contract Would Pay Each Season," showing 30% of each NBA season's salary cap in millions of dollars, from 1990-91 to 2026-27. Gold bars rise from left to right, each labeled with its value.

Values by season: 1990-91 3.6, 1991-92 3.8, 1992-93 4.2, 1993-94 4.6, 1994-95 4.8, 1995-96 6.9, 1996-97 7.4, 1997-98 8.1, 1998-99 9.0, 1999-00 10.2, 2000-01 10.7, 2001-02 12.8, 2002-03 12.1, 2003-04 13.2, 2004-05 13.2, 2005-06 14.8, 2006-07 15.9, 2007-08 16.7, 2008-09 17.6, 2009-10 17.3, 2010-11 17.4, 2011-12 17.4, 2012-13 17.4, 2013-14 17.6, 2014-15 18.9, 2015-16 21.0, 2016-17 28.2, 2017-18 29.7, 2018-19 30.6, 2019-20 32.7, 2020-21 32.7, 2021-22 33.7, 2022-23 37.1, 2023-24 40.8, 2024-25 42.2, 2025-26 46.4, 2026-27 49.5.

Growth is steady through the 1990s and 2000s, then flat at about 17 to 18 million from 2008-09 to 2013-14. The largest single-season jump comes in 2016-17, from 21.0 to 28.2 million. Values climb to a high of 49.5 million in 2026-27, nearly 14 times the 1990-91 figure.

Data: Spotrac. Viz: @hoopinformatics.com on Bluesky.

quote.author: Matt Norlander
quote.text:
